title: *MGT211 GDB*
text:
*MGT211 GDB*

*Scenario 1*
*Type of Company:* Private Limited Company
*Reason:* A Private Limited Company is suitable because it provides limited liability to shareholders while allowing Kamran and his cousins to maintain control of the business within their family. The transfer of shares to outsiders is restricted, and the company cannot offer its shares to the general public. Therefore, it is ideal for keeping ownership and management within the family.

*Scenario 2*
*Type of Company:* Not-for-Profit Company (Section 42 Company)
*Reason:* A Section 42 Not-for-Profit Company is suitable because it provides a separate legal identity and limited liability while working for educational and social welfare purposes. All profits and income must be used to achieve the company's objectives, and dividends cannot be distributed among founders or members. Therefore, it is ideal for providing free digital literacy to rural students through donations and public grants.

title: *MGT211 GDB*
text:
*MGT211 GDB* 

*Forms of Business Ownership* 

Course: Introduction to Business (MGT211)

 *1. Private Limited Company* 

This is the most suitable form of company for Kamran and his three cousins. It will provide limited liability and protect their personal assets from business debts. It will also allow them to keep control of the business within the family. The transfer of shares to outsiders can be restricted, and there is no need to offer shares to the general public. Therefore, a private limited company is the best choice for their business.

2. Company Limited by Guarantee (Section 42 Company)

This is the most suitable form of company for the educators. It provides a separate legal identity and limited liability to its members. It is formed for non-profit purposes and does not allow profits or dividends to be distributed among its members. All funds generated through donations and grants must be used for the organization's objectives. Therefore, a Section 42 company is suitable for providing free digital literacy to rural students.
